name: Haydn Taylor
highlight: A Cleethorpes dentist crossed on his first attempt in 1935. The registers and Dover’s swim log disagree by ten minutes.
biography: Haydn Taylor (1897–1962) was a dentist from Cleethorpes, Lincolnshire. He swam the Humber in 1932. A newspaper cutting in the Dover archive shows him with teammate Eddie Stockwood and coach Mr McNally.

On 22 August 1935 Taylor set out from Cap Gris-Nez at 01:35. Swimming crawl, he crossed to the cliffs west of Dover on his first attempt. Stockwood accompanied him over the final stretch. The Channel Swimming Association lists 14 hours 38 minutes. Dover’s account places his landing ten minutes later than the federation register does.

crossings.title: Cap Gris-Nez to the Dover coast, 22 August 1935

lines.label: Route
lines.text: France to England, solo. The dated archive log names Lydden Spout. Its reproduced newspaper report describes the landing as Abbot’s Cliff.

lines.label: Registered time
lines.text: 14 hours 38 minutes. The CS&PF historical record attributes ratification to the CSA.

lines.label: Clocks
lines.text: Both accounts give 01:35 for departure. The CS&PF record gives 16:13 at the finish. The Dover log gives 16:23 and 14 hours 48 minutes. Neither source specifies a time standard.

lines.label: Escort
lines.text: Dover’s swim log names E. Stone as pilot of Ocean King and J. Brockman as observer. It lists G. Obree, V. M. Whorlow and T. Brockman as crew.

lines.label: Archival account
lines.text: Channel Swimming Dover credits Taylor with the first crossing by a man. A cutting catalogued on 16 August shows Taylor with Stockwood and McNally. The precise swim date, course and elapsed time remain unconfirmed.

questions.label: How long did Haydn Taylor take to swim the English Channel?
questions.value: The CSA lists 14 hours 38 minutes. The Dover log gives 14 hours 48 minutes.

questions.label: Where did Haydn Taylor land?
questions.value: The Dover log names Lydden Spout, on the English coast between Dover and Folkestone.

questions.label: Who piloted Taylor’s Channel swim?
questions.value: The Dover archive names E. Stone on Ocean King.
